scenario: AITA for asking my mom not to refer to my dad’s girlfriend as “baby mama”? | Throwaway because I’ve said some identifying stuff on my main account. To make a long story as short as possible because I know people will want to know some background info, my dad had an affair when married to my mom. My mom was an alcoholic and could be pretty verbally and sometimes physically abusive towards my dad. Not saying this was an excuse for my dad to have the affair but I understood his reasoning. It was a messy spilt. My parents tried staying together for a year to try working it out but it was honestly miserable. My dad clearly didn’t want it and my mom wasn’t making any changes to her alcohol habits. My mom found out my dad was continuing the affair. 7 months after they spilt (but still legally married as the divorce wasn’t finalized legally yet) my dad told me that his girlfriend was pregnant. My mom found out and as expected she didn’t handle it too well. Over 5 years later, I have a half-brother I adore. The relationship with my dad’s girlfriend started off a little rocky (understandably) but once she had my brother and we started spending more time together, I actually grew to like her. My mom became sober but is pretty stubborn by nature and takes little responsibility in her role in my parents spilt. She’s become civil with my dad but still despises my dads girlfriend. I understand and she’s entitled to feel that way. But the issue is she’ll bad talk my dad’s girlfriend in front of me. My mom won’t even say her name and often refers to her as “baby mama”. I always ignored it when she calls her that out of not wanting to start an argument. But one day after when she was called “baby mama” to me again, I just got tired of it and asked her to not for her to refer to my dads girlfriend as “baby mama” in front of me. My mom was MAD. She said that “I was sticking up for her” after what she did to my mom. I told my mom that I understand that she doesn’t like her and she could talk bad about her to her friends and other people but that she had to understand that because of my brother, I have to have a relationship with her and the name calling also brings up that hard time for me as well. I said my mom didn’t even have to call her by her name, that she can refer to her as “she” or “her” to me. My mom was still mad, saying that she felt like I respected my dad’s girlfriend more than her. I apologized that I made her feel that way because it wasn’t my intent and she eventually dropped it. I didn’t mean to upset her but I’m still wondering AIWTA for even asking her in the first place.

message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether it's right or wrong for me to ask my mom not to refer to my dad's girlfriend as "baby mama." Let me start by understanding the situation better. My dad had an affair while he was married to my mom. My mom had some issues with alcohol and was sometimes verbally and even physically abusive towards my dad. I'm not saying that excuses the affair, but I can see why he might have been tempted. It was a messy situation. They tried to stay together for a year, but it was really miserable. My dad didn't want to stay, and my mom wasn't changing her habits. Then, my mom found out that my dad was still having the affair. Seven months after they split (but still legally married because the divorce wasn't finalized yet), my dad told me that his girlfriend was pregnant. My mom found out and didn't handle it well. Five years later, I have a half-brother I adore. The relationship with my dad's girlfriend started off a bit rocky, but once she had my brother and we started spending more time together, I actually grew to like her. My mom became sober but is pretty stubborn and doesn't take much responsibility for her role in my parents' split. She's civil with my dad but still despises his girlfriend. I understand that she's entitled to her feelings, but the issue is that she badmouths my dad's girlfriend in front of me. She won't even say her name and often refers to her as "baby mama." I always ignored it to avoid starting an argument. But one day, after she called her that again, I got tired of it and asked her not to refer to my dad's girlfriend as "baby mama" in front of me. My mom was MAD. She said I was sticking up for her after what she did to my mom. I told my mom that I understand she doesn't like her and she could talk bad about her to her friends and other people, but she had to understand that because of my brother, I have to have a relationship with her. The name-calling also brings up those hard times for me as well. I said my mom didn't even have to call her by her name; she could refer to her as "she" or "her" in front of me. My mom was still mad, saying she felt like I respected my dad's girlfriend more than her. I apologized for making her feel that way because it wasn't my intent, and she eventually dropped it. I didn't mean to upset her, but I still wonder if I overstepped by asking her in the first place. So, is it right or wrong for me to ask my mom not to refer to my dad's girlfriend as "baby mama"? Let me think about this. First, I need to consider the dynamics of the family. My mom and dad split under difficult circumstances, and my mom is still dealing with the aftermath. She's despising my dad's girlfriend, which is understandable given the situation. However, her badmouthing and using derogatory terms like "baby mama" in front of me is problematic. I have to balance my respect for my mom with my need to maintain a positive relationship with my dad's girlfriend, especially since she's the mother of my half-brother. I don't want to be in the middle of their conflict, but I also don't want to be exposed to negative talk about someone who is important to me. When I asked my mom not to refer to her as "baby mama," I was trying to set a boundary to protect myself and maintain a healthy relationship with my dad's girlfriend. However, my mom took it as me taking sides, which hurt her feelings. Is it right to set such a boundary? On one hand, it's important to stand up for what you need and protect your emotional well-being. On the other hand, it's also important to respect your parents and try to maintain harmony in the family. I think the key here is communication. I tried to explain my perspective and why I needed her to stop using that term. I also offered alternative ways for her to refer to my dad's girlfriend, showing that I was trying to be understanding. However, my mom felt disrespected, which led to her anger. It's possible that she felt that I was prioritizing my relationship with my dad's girlfriend over her, which is a sensitive issue. In the end, I apologized for making her feel that way and she eventually dropped it. So, in a way, I handled the situation as best as I could under the circumstances. But I'm still wondering if it was the right thing to do. Did I overstep by asking her to change how she refers to my dad's girlfriend? Or was it reasonable to set that boundary to protect myself and my relationship with my half-brother? I think it's a tough situation because family dynamics are complicated, and there's no perfect way to handle it. However, standing up for your emotional well-being and trying to maintain respectful communication is important. Even though it led to some conflict, it's better to address the issue than to let it fester. In conclusion, while it's understandable that my mom felt hurt, I believe it was right to set that boundary to protect myself and my relationship with my dad's girlfriend. It's a difficult balance, but communication and respect are key.
